# Creating a Photo Service A **service** is a reusable connection to a photo service: Yaffo knows how to talk to it, and every sync that uses it shares that knowledge. Build one when the service you want is missing from **Import from…** or **Send to…**. A service and a sync are different things. The service says how photos travel — which endpoints, which sign-in, which options. A sync says *which* photos travel and when it runs, and it records its own history. You publish the service once, then create as many syncs from it as you like. This walkthrough sends selected photos to Flickr sets as its example. You can describe another service, or an import instead — the steps are the same, only the direction you ask for differs. Flickr is not the point: the builder writes code either way, and the tabs you inspect are the same five. ## Before You Start Save a model and its provider key in [Settings → AI Generation](../reference-maintenance/settings.md#ai-generation). The builder writes the connection from your description, and it uses that model to do it. Without a key the chat stores nothing: the message is refused, and a notification reads **No API key configured. Add your Anthropic API key in Settings → AI Generation.** (the provider named is whichever model is active). Nothing is lost — add the key and send the same message again. ## Build the Service
### Choose Add a New Service Open **Library** → **Automations** and click **New automation**. The dialog asks what kind of automation you want; choose **Add a new service…**. It is the choice that builds a reusable connection rather than a sync. Give it the name you will recognise later, such as **Flickr exports**, and click **Create**. ![The new automation dialog with Add a new service selected and a name typed](assets/photo-services/new-photo-service.webp) ### Describe the Connection The builder opens on a draft. Say which service it is and which way photos travel — for this example: *Send selected photos to Flickr sets. Let me choose a destination set.* Include the options you need, such as choosing a set or keeping captions. The page has two halves. The left is the conversation: every message, the builder's replies, and any request it needs you to answer, drawn as a card. The right is five tabs over the draft. The header says **Draft** until you publish, so nothing here is used by a sync yet; a service you already published says **Published** even while a newer draft is open. ![The service builder with its conversation and the Overview tab](assets/photo-services/service-builder.webp) ### Check the Overview The **Overview** tab summarizes the draft: **Name**, **Direction** (**Imports photos** or **Sends photos**), **Sign-in**, **Hosts**, the **Options** it offers, and **Used by**, the number of syncs on the service. A send service also lists what it **Can** do — **Add**, **Remove**, **Captions**, **Recover** — and its **Batch size**. ![The Overview tab with direction, sign-in, hosts, options and capabilities](assets/photo-services/service-overview.webp) Read the direction first. If it is wrong, say so in the chat rather than building on it: everything after this — endpoints, test, publish — assumes it. ### Add App Credentials and a Test Account The **Account** tab appears once the builder knows how the service signs in, and holds the two things a connection needs. ![The Account tab with the callback URL, app credentials and the test account](assets/photo-services/service-account.webp) **App credentials** appears when the service wants to know which application is asking. Register an app with the photo service, and paste the return address the tab shows — here **Callback URL** — into the app's own configuration; it is the address the service sends the browser back to after sign-in. Then save the client ID and secret the app gives you (the service's own words for them, such as **Key** and **Secret**) with **Save credentials**. These identify Yaffo's app, not you, and every sync using this service reuses them; saving different ones later signs those syncs out. They live in your system keychain, not in Yaffo's database, and they are never sent to the AI model. **Test account** is the account the builder's tests read from. For a service with its own sign-in page the button stays disabled until the app credentials are saved, then signs you in; for a service that takes a key or a password, fill in the address (for a server of your own), the username and app password, or the API key, then click **Connect**. The account is stored like any other sign-in, so a sync you set up with this service later finds it already signed in. Change it with **Sign in again**. If the builder asked to make live read-only calls while you were talking to it and you allowed it, a **Live reads allowed** chip appears here with **Revoke**. Revoking stops the builder reading the account on its own; the responses it already read went to the AI model. **Test** is unaffected — you can always run a test yourself. ### Read the Access List The **Access** tab lists every web call the static check found in the draft, each with its method, its URL, and whether it **Reads** or **Writes**. Nothing outside this list can be called, and this is exactly the list **Publish** grants. ![The Access tab listing the draft's endpoints and their risks](assets/photo-services/service-access.webp) Read it before you publish. A send service needs writes, but only the ones it actually uses: a call you do not recognize here will be granted, so delete it from the conversation before publishing rather than after. ### Inspect the Code The **Code** tab is the draft itself. You do not have to read it, but it answers questions the summary cannot, and after the first publish a line above it reads **Differs from the published version** whenever the draft has moved on — that is the comparison that tells you a publish is pending. ![The Code tab with the draft and the differs-from-published note](assets/photo-services/service-code.webp) ### Test the Draft The **Test** tab runs the draft once against the test account. Fill in any options first, then click **Test**. Reads are live: the service's real answers come back, which is what makes the test worth running. Writes are recorded and never sent — the test does not upload, change, or delete anything. ![The Test tab with its option fields and the Test button](assets/photo-services/service-test.webp) For an option that names something at the far end, such as a set or an album, leave the field empty for the first run to list the choices the account has, then test again with one id from the results. Read the result, then describe any problem to the builder in the conversation. The builder sees the result with your next message, so you do not need to retype it. Repeat until the draft behaves as you expect. ### Publish **Publish** appears in the header once the draft passes its check and differs from what is published. It opens a review headed **Publish this service?** that lists the endpoints publication will grant, each marked **reads** or **changes things**. ![The publish review listing the endpoints it will grant](assets/photo-services/service-publish-review.webp) Approve it to make the draft the version syncs run. ### Create a Sync With It Go back to **New automation**. A published send service is now listed under **Send to…**, and a published import service under **Import from…**, beside the services that ship with Yaffo. ![New automation with Send to selected and the published service in the list](assets/photo-services/new-sync-send-to.webp) Choose it and complete the account, photo selection, options and setup review described in [Automations](automations.md). Publishing the service alone copies nothing: the service is the connection, and the sync you create from it is what moves photos.
## While the Builder Works While it works the builder may ask to read documentation on a domain it has not seen before. The request appears in the conversation as a card listing the domains; allow the ones you trust, or deny the request and describe the service from what you already know. A denied domain is not asked about again. It may also ask to make live read-only calls to the test account — allowing that lets it check its own guesses against real answers while it writes; see **Revoke** under [Add App Credentials and a Test Account](#add-app-credentials-and-a-test-account). ## Draft and Published A service keeps two versions side by side. The **published** version is what syncs run. The **draft** is what you and the builder are editing. Existing syncs keep running the published version while you work on the draft, which is why a draft can be in pieces, or fail its check, without breaking them. The tabs inspect the draft. Each is a separate page load, so reload or click the tab again after the builder answers to see the new state. A service stays in the **Services** section of the Automations panel, drafts included, with a **Draft** chip until it is published. Select it there to carry on editing. ## Update or Remove the Service **Regenerate** appears in the header when a published service no longer passes the current version's checks — after an app upgrade, usually — and the page says so above the tabs. It asks the builder to rebuild the service, keeping what it does and its direction, and to fix the problems listed. Syncs using the service are paused until it passes again. **Delete** removes the service and its stored app credentials. It is unavailable while a sync still uses the service: delete that sync first, then delete the service. ## When Something Does Not Work
### The Chat Will Not Send A notification naming a provider means no key is saved for the active model. Add it in [Settings → AI Generation](../reference-maintenance/settings.md#ai-generation) and send the message again — nothing was stored, so the draft is where you left it. A message that says the builder is already working means a run is still open: wait for it, or cancel it from the conversation, then send again.
### There Is No Publish Button **Publish** appears only when the draft passes its static check and differs from what is published. A warning above the tabs lists what failed; the draft was still saved, so describe the problem in the chat and let the builder fix it in place. On a service you have already published, a draft that changes the direction is refused — syncs depend on it — so keep the direction and change only the calls and options.
### Delete Is Unavailable **Delete** is greyed out while a sync uses the service, and the page says so if you get past it: **A sync still uses this service. Delete that sync first.** Delete the sync under **Syncs** in the Automations panel, then delete the service. To keep the service but stop using it, disable the sync instead.
files.description: The photo-services page: a guided walkthrough build (dialog, builder, Overview, Account, Access, Code, Test, publish review, Send to), then prose on permissions, draft versus published, regenerate and delete, and a troubleshooting chooser.

Captures the seeded Flickr-exports draft's builder, its five tabs, the publish review and the Send-to dialog entry; drives the chat, permission, account, and delete/regenerate routes for dependencies.

pageContext: Fixture: the docs sandbox seeds one service, published 'Flickr exports' at /utilities/automations/services/custom.flickr-exports, with a NEWER unpublished draft on top (header says Published, Code tab says 'Differs from the published version.', Publish is offered, used_by = 0 so the publish review shows no wider-access sentence and Delete is enabled). Do not delete it — every shot on the page reads it. Tab state lives only in ?tab=overview|account|web|code|test, so pin the tab in the URL; there is nothing else server-persisted in the URL. Account tab: app credentials NOT saved, so 'Sign in to Flickr exports' is disabled and there is no 'Live reads allowed' chip and no Saved chip — the fixture cannot show a signed-in test account or a live-reads chip, which is why the page describes both in prose. The callback URL renders as http://127.0.0.1:5002 (loopback, no path) because metadata connection.redirect == 'registered'. The Test tab has one option field (Flickr set, remote_collection) and an empty #service-test-result div; a real result needs a live Flickr account, so never picture one. The publish modal (#servicePublishModal) only opens via JS on #service-publish after html[data-app-ready]; the New automation dialog only enables its service radios after the page script runs, so click the label.choice-card rather than the input. Code tab's pre.automation-code caps itself at ~504px and scrolls, so a .service-panel crop is bounded. The Pages strip (#nav-pages-toggle / #navbar-pages-bar) is a global server-persisted preference, collapsed by default; the walkthrough pins it collapsed for the two modal shots and restores it. NOT VERIFIED: I ran out of tool budget before confirming the composed crops by eye (service-builder.webp's .utilities-content crop was carried over from the previous run and is probably right, but the six .service-panel crops and both modal crops at clipPadding 0 were chosen from measured boxes only).
explanation: Read the page, its memories and the existing walkthrough, then read yaffo/routes/utilities/sync_services.py and templates/utilities/sync_service.html for the five tabs, the Publish modal and the header actions, and templates/utilities/_base.html for the New automation dialog. Drove the running sandbox to confirm the fixture: the seeded 'Flickr exports' service is published with an unpublished draft (Publish button present, Code tab shows 'Differs from the published version.', 198 lines of code capped at a 504px scroll box), its Account tab shows the unsaved app-credentials form with a loopback Callback URL and a disabled 'Sign in to Flickr exports', its Access tab lists GET api.flickr.com (Reads) plus POST api.flickr.com and POST up.flickr.com (Writes), its Test tab has one 'Flickr set' option and the Test button, and #servicePublishModal carries the endpoint list marked reads / changes things with used_by = 0 so no wider-access sentence. The dialog's Send to group already lists the published service, and its radios are disabled until the page script selects the kind — so the walkthrough clicks the choice card, not the input. Rewrote the page around the walkthrough the spec demands: eight steps, one screenshot each (dialog, builder+Overview, Overview, Account, Access, Code, Test, publish review, Send to), with permissions, draft-versus-published, Regenerate/Delete and the troubleshooting chooser left as prose outside it. Nothing outside the walkthrough is an annotated screenshot because the page has no non-step screenshot left to annotate. Flows drive the permission-answer route (409 on the already-resolved message), the chat route (400 without a key), the disabled test-account button, the Regenerate-absent / Delete-enabled header state, and the Send to list.
